sources.entry: GeneWeb - Genealogy software that can be used offline or as a Web service. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 OCaml

summary.one_liner: GeneWeb is open-source genealogy software written in OCaml that can run locally or as a web server, with a browser-based interface.
summary.what_it_does: GeneWeb is genealogy software with a web interface, written in OCaml, created by Daniel de Rauglaudre in 1998. It can be run locally on a personal computer or deployed as a web server. The README says it handles databases with millions of individuals and can find relationships between people across many possible paths. It supports granular access controls intended to protect information about living persons. It provides full GEDCOM import and export and uses its own .gw database format. The README also mentions a Google Colab option for trying it in a browser without installation.
use_cases: Maintain a family tree on your own computer
Host a genealogy database as a web service
Import and export family data in GEDCOM format
Find relationship paths between individuals in large family trees
Restrict visibility of living persons in a shared family database
Try genealogy software in a browser without installing
how_to_run: Linux: run ./gwd.sh in a terminal, then open the browser at the address shown
notable: Engine behind Roglo (over 11 million individuals) and formerly Geneanet
Granular access controls for living persons' data
Runs offline on a desktop or as a web server
caveats: Version 7.1 is labeled beta because its internal database format is not yet compatible with Geneanet's infrastructure
Back up databases in .gw format before installing a new version
On Unix, binding to port 80 requires elevated privileges or capabilities; macOS needs launchd to redirect port 80 to 2317
